claims.text: Predator-proofing is the most imoprtant aspect for safety: use robust chicken wire, bury the fence in to the ground around the perimeter against foxes, and use an automatic door that closes at dusk.
claims.span: Predator-proofing is the most imoprtant aspect for safety: use robust chicken wire, bury the fence in to the ground around the perimeter against foxes, and use an automatic door that closes at dusk.

claims.text: Provide the chickens with designated chicken feed that contains important vitamins and minerals. Provide clean water available 24/7. Clean the waterers often and thouroughly to stop algae and mould.

claims.text: Add some absorbent bedding like pine shavings (around 4-6 inches), and replace it weekly, top it up as needed. Offer 1 nesting box per 3/4 hens and 8-12 inches of roosting bar per bird will help them feel safe and comfy.

claims.text: Finally, it is important to check the flock daily so you understand what "normal" behavior looks like for each hen, quarantine any new birds for 7-10 days before introduction to avoid spread of illness and parasites, and compost manure before it goes anywhere near the vegetable beds.
